newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: ICN to open new plant in Montenegro.
newsitem.headline: ICN to open new plant in Montenegro.

text.p: ICN Pharmaceuticals Inc will soon expand its Yugoslav operations with a new drug factory in Podgorica, capital of the republic of Montenegro, an ICN Yugoslavia executive director said on Tuesday.
"The plant...will operate under the name ICN Montenegro," Mihajlo Saranovic, executive vice-president and manager for East European operations, told Reuters.
The Costa Mesa, Calif.-based parent company will have a 75 percent stake in the new venture. The rest will be held by the Montenegrin state.

The contract for the plant, to produce 19 medicines earmarked for Yugoslav and foreign markets, was signed on Monday by Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic and ICN Yugoslavia executive vice president Ljubisa Rakic.
"This will become a medium-sized drug plant, producing according to FDA and the European Union standards," Saranovic said.
The new plant in Podgorica plans to reach $20 million sales by the end of 1997. In 1999 it targets $32 million sales, he said.
ICN Yugoslavia was set up as a joint venture with Yugoslav firm Galenika in 1991.
Formerly operating under the name ICN Galenika, the Belgrade-based company will provide help to the Montenegrin plant over next few months until the new factory is fully equipped, Saranovic said.
ICN Yugoslavia earlier said its 1996 annual sales were expected to reach nearly $350 million, bringing substantial net income to the parent company.
ICN Pharmaceuticals owns 75 percent of the shares in the Yugoslav subsidiary, which it describes as its "window to eastern Europe".

"We are already a leader among western pharmaceutical companies in eastern Europe after the recent acquisition of three companies in Russia, one in Hungary and one in Kazakhstan," an ICN official said.
ICN Pharmaceuticals will soon set up a joint stock company with Ohis of Skopje, under the name ICN Macedonia.
It has also signed a letter of intent to form a joint limited liability company ICN Bosnia with Krajinalek from Banja Luka in the Bosnian Serb entity.
The California-based parent company will have majority stakes in all future joint ventures.
